name: Sample block: 5K base
coachNotes: A gentle 4-week base block: mostly easy running, one quality session a week and a slowly growing long run. Targets here use effort only because a sample can't know your paces or heart rate; your AI-generated plan will give you exact numbers.

glossary.meaning: Rate of Perceived Exertion: how hard a run feels on a 1-10 scale. 1 is standing still, 3 is easy chatting, 7 is hard but controlled, 10 is an all-out sprint.
An easy heart-rate range, roughly 60-70% of your max heart rate. You can talk in full sentences. Most of your running should be here because it builds endurance without wearing you out.
Short, smooth accelerations of about 20 seconds up to a fast but relaxed pace, followed by a full recovery. They practise good form and leg speed without being tiring.
A sustained 'comfortably hard' effort (RPE 6-7), about the pace you could race for an hour. You can say a few words but not hold a conversation. It raises the pace you can keep up for a long time.
Short hard efforts (reps) separated by easy recovery jogs or walks. Splitting the hard running into pieces lets you spend more time at a fast pace than you could in one go.
A solo, race-effort run over a set distance to measure your current fitness. It gives you and your coach a benchmark to plan from.

runs.title: Easy run
runs.purpose: Builds your aerobic base, the foundation that every faster session sits on.
keyPoints: Keep it easy enough to chat the whole way
Walk breaks are fine if your breathing gets heavy

segments.label: Easy run
segments.targetEffort: RPE 3/10, can talk in full sentences
segments.instructions: Start slower than feels natural. If you can't speak a full sentence, slow down.

runs.title: Easy run + strides
runs.purpose: Easy aerobic running, plus strides at the end to wake up your legs and practise good running form.
keyPoints: The easy part stays easy
Strides are fast but relaxed, never a sprint

segments.label: Strides

recoveryStep.label: Walk back
recoveryStep.instructions: Walk back to where you started, about 60 s

segments.instructions: Build up over 5 s, hold a quick relaxed pace, then ease off. Stand tall with quick, light feet and relaxed shoulders.

runs.title: Long run
runs.purpose: Your longest run of the week builds endurance and gets your body used to time on your feet.
keyPoints: Distance matters more than pace today
Run the first half slower than the second

segments.label: Long easy run
segments.instructions: Steady and easy. Take walk breaks whenever you need them.

runs.title: Easy run
runs.purpose: More aerobic base, slightly longer than last week.
keyPoints: Conversational effort the whole way

runs.title: Minute repeats
runs.purpose: Your first intervals session: short, hard efforts that build speed and teach you how 5K effort feels.
keyPoints: Run every rep at the same effort; don't blast the first one
The recovery jog really is easy

segments.label: Warm-up
segments.instructions: Easy jog, building gently over the last few minutes.

segments.label: Hard minutes
segments.instructions: Hard but controlled: you should be able to do one more rep at the end.

runs.title: Long run
runs.purpose: Extends your endurance by another kilometre.
keyPoints: Easy pace, walk breaks are fine

runs.title: Easy run
runs.purpose: Aerobic base, now 30 minutes non-stop if you can.
keyPoints: Conversational effort the whole way

runs.title: Tempo
runs.purpose: Raises the pace you can hold for a long time, which is what makes a 5K feel easier.
keyPoints: Comfortably hard, not racing
Keep the pace even for the full 15 minutes

segments.label: Tempo
segments.targetEffort: RPE 6-7/10, a few words at a time
segments.instructions: Settle into a rhythm in the first 2 minutes, then hold it. If it gets too hard to keep going, ease off slightly.

runs.title: Long run
runs.purpose: The longest run of the block.
keyPoints: Easy pace, walk breaks are fine
Take water if it's warm

runs.title: Recovery run
runs.purpose: A lighter week lets your body absorb the training so you come out of it fitter.
keyPoints: Slower than your normal easy pace
Feeling fresh afterwards is the goal

runs.title: Hill reps
runs.purpose: Builds leg strength and running power with less impact than fast running on the flat.
keyPoints: Drive with your arms and lift your knees
Jog back down slowly; that's your recovery

segments.label: Warm-up
segments.instructions: Jog to a moderate hill that takes at least 30 s to run up.

segments.label: Uphill

recoveryStep.label: Easy jog
recoveryStep.instructions: Easy jog or walk back down

segments.instructions: Lean slightly forward from the ankles, short quick steps, look up the hill.

runs.title: 5K time trial
runs.purpose: Measures your current 5K fitness so the next block's paces and heart-rate targets are based on real numbers.
keyPoints: Run as evenly as you can; don't start too fast
Wear your Apple Watch so the data reaches your coach

segments.label: 5K time trial
segments.instructions: First kilometre controlled, middle kilometres steady, then push the last kilometre.
